_comment: What the host did with a hook output, observed by emitting one and reading the verdict.
`codex exec` prints `hook: <Event> Completed` or `hook: <Event> Failed` per firing, which
is the whole signal: the host either took the output or it did not. Each entry below is
one probe -- one output shape, emitted from every registered event in a single session,
with the verdict recorded per event.
This is the externally-verified half of `codex-output-rules.json`. That table states what
this plugin must not emit; the entries here are the subset of it a run of the real binary
has actually confirmed. `codex-payload.test.mjs` cross-checks the two, so the contract
cannot drift away from the observation without a test saying so.
Only events that fire in the probe session appear. `PermissionRequest`, `PreCompact`,
`PostCompact`, `SubagentStart` and `SubagentStop` need a session shape the probe does not
reach, so they are absent rather than assumed -- see `payloads/README.md`.
